name: Malicious LiteLLM PyPI releases 1.82.7 and 1.82.8
summary: The LiteLLM package was compromised and malicious PyPI versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 were published with secret-exfiltration behavior.

name: LiteLLM MCP OAuth2 Passthrough Authentication Bypass
summary: A fallback in LiteLLM MCP authentication could allow requests with an arbitrary Bearer token to reach configured MCP tooling without a valid LiteLLM key.

name: LiteLLM MCP Proxy Improper Authentication
summary: LiteLLM MCP proxy authentication logic was affected by improper authentication and fixed in 1.84.0.

name: LiteLLM Custom Code Guardrails Production Safety-Check Bypass
summary: Production create/update paths for custom-code guardrails did not apply the same sandboxing and validation as the test path, enabling code execution under specified privilege conditions.

name: Trivy Ecosystem Supply-Chain Compromise
affected: compromised Trivy release/action ecosystem during incident window
summary: A compromised credential was used to publish malicious Trivy ecosystem artifacts and mutable action references during the March 2026 incident.

name: Trivy Crafted OCI Artifact Path Traversal
summary: A crafted OCI artifact title could cause Trivy to write downloaded layer content outside the intended destination when fetching attacker-controlled artifacts.

name: Semantic Kernel In-Memory Vector Store filter injection to RCE
summary: Prompt injection could reach unsafe string interpolation in Python lambda filters executed via eval(), turning a data lookup into code execution. Microsoft did not publish a CVSS score in the cited post.

name: Semantic Kernel SessionsPythonPlugin arbitrary file access
summary: A helper (DownloadFileAsync) was exposed to the model with unvalidated path parameters, allowing model-controlled file read/write outside the intended sandbox.

name: MCP STDIO configuration command injection across AI frameworks
summary: OX Security reports that unsanitized STDIO server parameters let attacker-influenced MCP configuration execute OS commands across SDK-derived products. Several vendors disputed the finding as intended behaviour of the transport; only identifiers corroborated by more than one source are listed here.
